answer: Nectar-Ledger Cross-Validation. Each identity must submit a private, locally computed random seed whose derived work is validated by independent neighbors; seeds are logged like a raven's cache so reuse across identities surfaces as an identical ledger entry. An attacker duplicating identities must generate a fresh, distinguishable seed per instance and get it independently confirmed, so each clone costs a separate validation round plus distinct compute and neighbor attention. Collusion clusters drift into a nebula of overlapping confirmation paths that the ledger flags as shared work.
